correctness.rationale: A linearly ordered n-element carrier has n−1 directed reference edges, and each has exactly one two-coordinate profile, measured only in orders 2 and 3. The two Cartesian squares respectively force 9 and 16 edges, giving lower bounds 10 and 17 and the exact once-per-profile census at equality. The independent inverse-permutation witness check reproduces all 9 and 16 profiles on the stated witnesses (and the listed profile tables agree with the position differences). Appending fresh elements to the end of all three orders preserves both adjacencies and gaps between every old pair and hence every realized profile. The conjunction of existential pair formulas uses two nested quantifiers and quantifier-free tests in the corresponding signatures. No claim is made about a language that must axiomatize linear orders and their successors on arbitrary structures at rank two.
residual_risks: The finite checks certify the two witnesses; the edge count and end-extension argument establish the spectra, not a finite search for counterexamples.

evidence: The frozen descriptions identify general many-successor finite-model and decidability bounds, and a two-successor satisfiability result. The multitournament catalogue result uses freely chosen tournament directions, not successive elements of linear orders.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general logic framework can express the successor-only property without determining its exact minimum; a general finite-model upper bound does not give the specific sharp witness without additional argument. The order-visible formulation requires gap orientations and cannot be reduced merely by interpreting a successor relation as an arbitrary tournament.

value.rationale: This is an exact finite-model budget for two natural signatures on the same objects. Although the lower bounds are counts, attaining them is constrained by simultaneously realizing each profile with three spanning directed paths. The two witnesses show that these constraints impose no extra vertices, and isolate the cost of exposing the orientation of a nonadjacent pair. The formulas and extension argument make the results useful as small finite-model benchmarks.
residual_risks: No general satisfiability bound or classification of all minimizing models follows.
